articles.title: Giti Tire Names Michael Markoff Chief Operating Officer
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: Giti Tire USA has promoted Michael Markoff to chief operating officer, effective Nov. 1. The appointment comes as the company launches the Giti brand in the U.S. and builds on momentum for its GT Radial brand. Markoff previously served as executive vice president of sales and marketing. He reports to Dr. Enki Tan, executive chairman of Giti Tire.
In his expanded role, Markoff oversees sales, marketing, logistics, supply chain, technical service, industry relations and product development.

“I am honored to take on this role and build on the strong foundation our team has established,” said Markoff. “I look forward to working with our employees, customers, and partners to strengthen our operations, enhance customer service, and support Giti Tire USA’s continued growth.

During an exclusive interview at the SEMA Show, Markoff discussed his 29 years in the tire industry, including 26 with Goodyear in R&D, marketing and sales roles in the U.S. and Europe. He has also spent more than two years with Giti Tire.
“Moving from head of sales and marketing into chief operating officer [has] been an exciting opportunity,” he said. “We have a very strong team and we’re excited about the future.”

The promotion is part of a planned leadership transition. Phang Wai Yeen, formerly chief executive officer of Giti Tire’s North American operations, will now lead global research and development activities.
Read the full article on tirereview.com.

articles.title: SEMA Names Ryan Mascoli Chief Operations Officer
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: The Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) has named Ryan Mascoli chief operations officer (COO), effective Nov. 16. Mascoli brings more than 15 years of experience in operational strategy, business transformation and growth within manufacturing and supply chain organizations.
Reporting to SEMA CEO Mike Spagnola, he will oversee day-to-day operations and advance strategic initiatives. He also will align teams and resources with the association’s long-term priorities.

“Ryan is a proven operational leader who understands how to translate strategy into measurable results,” said Spagnola. “His experience will strengthen our executive team and help SEMA operate with greater alignment, accountability and effectiveness. By improving how we work across the organization, we will be better positioned to deliver meaningful value to our members and foster the success of the automotive aftermarket.”
SEMA Appointee Brings Manufacturing and Operations Experience

Mascoli most recently served as vice president of operations for Advanced Charging Technologies, leading enterprise operations across manufacturing, supply chain and production. During his tenure, the company grew revenue from $25 million to $60 million while maintaining a 99.6% on-time delivery rate.

He also increased daily production output by 25% and reduced order dwell time from 21 days to two days. Additionally, he led a companywide enterprise resource planning implementation that took three months to complete.
Previously, Mascoli served as general manager and COO at ICE Cable Systems. He oversaw finance, sales, supply chain, marketing, information technology and human resources.
From 2019 to 2021, the company grew revenue from $10 million to $22 million. It also increased profit from $200,000 to $3.7 million.
Earlier in his career, he held supply chain and inventory leadership positions at ICE Cable Systems and Toshiba.
Mascoli to Oversee Strategic Initiatives

“SEMA plays a vital role in creating the conditions for aftermarket businesses and professionals to succeed,” said Mascoli. “I look forward to working with SEMA’s leadership, staff, board and members to strengthen operations, execute strategic priorities and deliver greater value to the industry.”
As COO, Mascoli will establish performance measures, support annual planning and budgeting, improve organizational processes and help manage operational risks.

He also will work with department leaders to support employee development. Additionally, he will align organizational priorities with SEMA’s mission to foster the success of the automotive aftermarket.
Mascoli studied business administration with an emphasis in management at California State University, Fullerton.

articles.title: YANG Launches 2027 Mentorship Program
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: The Young Auto Care Network Group (YANG), a community of the Auto Care Association, recently launched its 2027 YANG Mentorship Program. Now in its fifth year, the program averages 125 mentees and 24 volunteer mentors annually. Anyone under age 40 who joins the YANG community can participate for free.

“One of the most valuable aspects of my involvement with YANG has been the relationships I’ve built with individuals who genuinely challenge me to grow, both personally and professionally,” said Brandon Crenshaw, chair, YANG. “The Mentorship Program creates an opportunity to go beyond networking, by building meaningful connections, challenging your own perspectives, and developing the confidence and perspective to lead in new ways. It’s an experience I encourage every young professional in our industry to embrace.”

Each mentorship circle consists of approximately five mentees and one mentor focused on a unique topic.

articles.title: NAPA Opens First Highly Automated Reverse Logistics Center
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: NAPA recently celebrated the grand opening of its York Reverse Logistics Center (RLC), marking the debut of the first highly automated facility of its kind within the NAPA network and an important milestone in the company’s ongoing supply chain transformation.

The 400,000-square-foot center combines more than 100 robots and advanced automation technology with a skilled local workforce to process returns, cores and inventory for redistribution across the NAPA Northeast distribution network.

The center began operations earlier this year and is designed to accelerate returns processing, helping get parts back into inventory faster and improving availability for NAPA stores, repair professionals and their customers, the company said. The new facility, which can support 250,000 unique SKUs, is expected to reduce the time needed to prepare inventory for redistribution by 43% and support inventory accuracy up to 99.5%.

Leaders from NAPA and corporate parent Genuine Parts Company (GPC) were joined by York Mayor Sandie Walker, state and local elected officials, the York County Economic Alliance, community partners and teammates for a ribbon-cutting ceremony and tours of the facility at 500 Willow Springs Lane.

“York is the first step in a broader modernization of the NAPA supply chain,” said Justin Ducharme, executive vice president, supply chain, NAPA. “By combining innovative technology with the expertise of our teammates, we’re creating a more efficient operation that helps keep parts moving to the customers and repair professionals who rely on us every day.”

During the ceremony, the GPC Foundation presented a $2,500 Good Neighbor grant to United Way of York County. The grant supports the foundation’s mobility priority and reflects a shared belief that reliable transportation opens access to jobs, health care and stronger family life.

As the first highly automated reverse logistics center within the NAPA network, RLC represents an important milestone in the company’s efforts to enhance operational capabilities and support the growing needs of customers across the Northeast, the company said.

articles.title: An Anthropic mathematician claims to have proven the Riemann hypothesis. We have to rethink how we reward expertise.
articles.author: Kit Yates

paras.en: An Anthropic mathematician using Claude claims to have proven the most famous problem in math — the Riemann hypothesis — in the latest, but potentially most consequential, example of artificial intelligence (AI) producing stunning math results.

AI has steamrolled its way into the math community. Anthropic's proof will certainly and rightly be scrutinized, but rather than picking apart every single result these models produce, we should respond by changing how we evaluate and reward expertise — placing less weight on the volume of results and more on the human judgment required to decide which questions and answers matter.
Without this shift, we risk drowning genuine insight in a flood of plausible but poorly understood mathematics.

Mathematical judgment is the ability to distinguish a result that is correct, but boring, from one that might fundamentally change how we think about the problem or even the whole area of mathematics surrounding the problem.

AI could generate hundreds of thousands of complex variations on a theorem, but these variations might add very little to mathematical knowledge, each one ultimately proving a dead end. A truly consequential result might settle a long-standing unsolved problem or connect to apparently unrelated areas. It is mathematical judgment that allows us to tell the difference between the two.

Earlier this year, an OpenAI system produced a counterexample to the long-standing planar unit distance problem, overturning a conjecture of Paul Erdős that had resisted mathematicians for decades. More recently, OpenAI announced an apparent solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, a celebrated question about whether equations describing fluid flow can develop singularities, or infinite values. It is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute's Millennium Prize Problems — a set of seven well-known and complex math problems, each with a $1 million prize attached.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Whether OpenAI's result ultimately stands up to scrutiny remains to be seen. But what is clear is that AI systems are now operating at a level that many mathematicians did not expect to witness for years, if not decades. OpenAI has since released hundreds of further mathematical results, leaving mathematicians scrambling to assess their correctness and significance.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
This does not mean that mathematicians are about to become obsolete. But it does mean we need to carefully reconsider what their precise purpose is.

Traditionally, expertise has been closely associated with production: Experts solve difficult problems, prove theorems, construct models and write papers. If AI can generate proofs, conjectures and probe research areas at unprecedented speed and scale, mathematical production is no longer necessarily the bottleneck. Instead, many pure mathematicians would argue that it is mathematical judgment that will become the scarcer resource.

Human judgment remains necessary because proofs generated by AI are not necessarily illuminating, comprehensible or even reliable. Some proofs may be so long or opaque that checking them requires substantial work by specialists and even more work to reinterpret them in a way that is meaningful to human mathematicians.

A proof can be valid without offering insight into why it is true or how its ideas might be employed elsewhere. The job of human mathematicians will be to become arbiters of the correctness of proofs, but also to scrutinize the reasoning and to extract the underlying ideas, determining whether the result says anything that meaningfully advances the field.

Mathematics, as a research community, needs to react rapidly to this change. Mathematicians and journals must prioritize significance over output. Mathematics involves deciding which results are important as well as generating them. A proof can be correct without being insightful. To give a simplified example, AI might "prove" that the square of a number divisible by two is divisible by four and then prove that the square of a number divisible by three is divisible by nine, and so on with ever larger integers. However, each new "proof" isn't an example of insightful mathematics, just a variation on the same elementary idea.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In contrast, a significant proof might settle a long-standing question, reveal an unexpected connection between disparate fields or develop a technique which is useful in the solution of many other problems.

Journals should therefore require authors to explain clearly what is genuinely new, why it matters — and what role AI played. Reviewers should judge whether a result deepens understanding, rather than merely verifying that the argument works. That does not mean rejecting work whose eventual importance is uncertain. The history of mathematics is full of ideas whose significance became apparent only decades later, so journals must continue to make room for foundational, exploratory and curiosity-driven research.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: But there is a difference between a result with as-yet unknown implications and one that is unlikely ever to be insightful. Mathematical judgement cannot guarantee that nothing valuable is ever overlooked. It can, however, distinguish work that contains genuinely new ideas or possibilities from the automated production of uninteresting dead ends.

Universities and funders should also stop treating publication counts as a convenient proxy for quality. Careers are built around papers, citations, grants and prizes, but these measures were developed when producing sophisticated mathematics demanded substantial human time and effort. In the age of AI, work that might previously have taken years of careful thought could now be produced in weeks or even days.

Consequently, as the cost of generating mathematical results falls dramatically, those measures of quality become less useful. A decreased reliance on traditional metrics may be no bad thing, but institutions need credible alternatives: assessments of a researcher's most important contributions, evidence of intellectual leadership and explanations of how their work has changed understanding. This is urgent because mathematicians are already struggling to evaluate the sheer volume of material being produced.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Finally, mathematical training must continue to reward understanding. Written work alone will become a less reliable guide to individual capability when papers, reports and applications can be written mostly using AI. Seminars, discussions and collaborations can reveal whether someone understands an argument, can defend it and can connect it to other ideas. Demonstrating understanding has always been a more important quality in university students than simply presenting the answer; education and recruitment should now reflect that principle more explicitly.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - AI is solving 'impossible' math problems. Can it best the world's top mathematicians?
- 'Everything we know about space travel is going to change within a decade': The fusion breakthrough that could unlock a path to the stars
- 'Why would you ruin your career?': OpenAI claims to have cracked one of math's greatest unsolved problems, but mathematicians allege it played dirty

Critics might argue that this is an overreaction. Mathematical claims still require proof, peer review already evaluates significance, and AI is simply another tool, like a calculator or computer algebra system. There is a degree of truth to each objection. Yet the explosion in the number of published papers changes the nature of the game. A calculator does not generate hundreds of research claims that specialists must spend precious time checking. AI can create arguments faster than the community can verify, interpret or absorb them. Existing safeguards were not designed for that imbalance.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Recent advances have understandably generated both excitement and anxiety. The right response is neither to reject AI nor to unguardedly celebrate every finding it produces. Journals, universities and funders should adapt their incentives now, before quantity overwhelms judgment completely.

In an environment increasingly capable of automatically generating research-level mathematics, the most valuable experts will be those who know which questions are worth asking, which results deserve trust and which ideas are worth our attention.

His science journalism has won awards from the Royal Statistical Society and The Conversation, and has written two popular science books, The Math(s) of Life and Death and How to Expect the Unexpected.

articles.title: James Webb telescope spots giant star swallowing its companion in first-ever observations of a stellar merger
articles.author: Joanna Thompson

paras.en: For the first time, astronomers have caught two stars — a supergiant and a star slightly smaller than the sun — in the act of merging. After orbiting each other for thousands of years, the pair came together in just under seven years — a span short enough that researchers could watch the drama play out from start to finish. The discovery was described in a study published Nov. 18 in the journal Nature.

"Stellar mergers are very, very difficult to observe in real time because they are hard to predict," Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University and first author of the study, said in a NASA statement. "However, we noticed something unusual was going on in 2023 and continued to monitor the system to see what it would do."

The stars' imminent merger was originally picked up by NASA's now-retired Near-Earth Object Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer — a spacecraft that was designed to spot asteroids but also discovered many other interesting changes in the night sky.

Researchers noticed that a previously stable binary star system in the Andromeda galaxy, the closest major galaxy to ours, had begun to brighten. Follow-up observations from the Wide-Field Infrared Transient Explorer — a near-infrared instrument at the Palomar Observatory in California — revealed that the galaxy had also started spewing dust. Karambelkar’s team backed up these observations with data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) in December 2025.

The researchers dubbed the binary pair "Bao" (after its formal name, AT 2025abao) and started keeping tabs. They found that sometime in 2018, the smaller component of Bao bumped into the surface of the supergiant Bao. From there, things escalated quickly. The stars started exchanging gas in a process known as common envelope evolution. The larger Bao dragged its smaller companion closer and closer, until it was finally sucked into the supergiant's core, releasing a gigantic burst of energy.
- 'A collision within a collision': Neutron star merger hiding in mini-galaxy could answer 2 big astrophysics questions
- Universe-shaking collision of black hole and neutron star could upend our understanding of monster cosmic mergers
- Never-before-seen 'strange quark star' may have formed after cosmic collision, physicists say
This dramatic culmination was "almost like a bomb exploding inside a living star," study co-author Kishalay De, an astronomer at Columbia University, said in the statement.

The researchers were surprised by not only the speed of this interaction but also its outcome. Bao could have easily exploded into a supernova, transformed into a neutron star or collapsed into a black hole. Instead, it seems to have settled back into a single massive star. Future observations will give scientists a sense of how the new, rejuvenated Bao is holding up after its act of cosmic cannibalism.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

The team's analysis could also help inform future studies of supergiant stars and binary systems. Getting a clearer picture of how common envelope evolution works could allow astronomers to reconstruct how previous mergers went down. Thanks to NASA's new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, Karambelkar predicts Bao will be far from the last merging stars scientists spot.

Joanna Thompson is a science journalist and runner based in New York. She holds a B.S. in Zoology and a B.A. in Creative Writing from North Carolina State University, as well as a Master's in Science Journalism from NYU's Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program. Find more of her work in Scientific American, The Daily Beast, Atlas Obscura or Audubon Magazine.

articles.title: Waterfall of fog spills over Mallorca cliffs in stunning winning image for Weather Photographer of the Year 2026
articles.author: Elise Poore

paras.en: The first light of dawn illuminates a sea of fog spilling over the rugged cliffs of Mallorca, Spain, in this year's winning Weather Photographer of the Year 2026 image. Photographer Francisco Bailón Rodríguez captured the scene from the Albercutz Watchtower, looking toward the Formentor Peninsula, after several days of high pressure and humid nights created the perfect conditions for fog to blanket the landscape.

On Nov. 17, the photograph, titled "Mares de Niebla (Seas of Fog)," was named overall winner of the Royal Meteorological Society's competition, which attracted more than 5,500 entries from photographers around the world.

The competition celebrates the ephemeral scenes created by weather, which can for brief moments transform landscapes into something extraordinary. Take a look at this year's winning photographs below and let us know your favorites in the comments.

Photographer Weilu Chen took second place in the main category with this spectacular image of golden light shining over the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge that runs for 34 miles (55 kilometers) across the Pearl River estuary in southern China.
"A Supercell in the Sandhills of Nebraska"

A striking bolt of lightning illuminates a horizontal cloud during a thunderstorm, earning third place in the main category. These clouds are called arcus clouds that have a distinct shelf-like shape. "Mother Nature was kind enough to give us a supercell and lightning at night," photographer Laura Hedien said in a statement.
"Misty Sunrise over the Long Coc Tea Hills"
Photographer Mahmudul Hasan won first place in the public vote category for this image of the rolling tea hills of Long Coc, Vietnam, emerging through layers of mist.
Watching from Bayonne, New Jersey, photographer Dan Martland captured this triple lightning strike above New York City, earning second place in the public vote category.

articles.title: For the First Time, Astronomers Witnessed a Giant Star Gobble Up Its Smaller Stellar Companion

paras.en: In 2023, astronomers realized that a red giant star in our neighboring Andromeda galaxy was doing something strange. Sure enough, two years later, the astronomical object exploded.

The researchers rushed to observe the phenomenon, and they sifted through older data to piece together what had happened. Analyses suggest the huge star had gobbled up its smaller stellar companion, marking the first direct observation of this kind of star merger. The findings were described November 18 in the journal Nature.

The eruption, called AT 2025abao, occurred because the two stars shared what’s called a common envelope. Some stars approaching the end of their lives balloon to a huge size, entering a giant phase. As an object expands, its outer layer of gas—or envelope—engulfs anything orbiting it, resulting in odd interactions.

However, common envelopes are tough to observe because they happen over relatively short timescales of months to years, and usually, just a few stars exist in this phase at a time within a galaxy, writes Jason Nordhaus, an astrophysicist at the Rochester Institute of Technology who did not participate in the work, in commentary accompanying the study.
Experts estimate that nearly a third of all stars go through a common envelope phase at some point during their lives, reports New Scientist.

To investigate the strange event, which occurred in October 2025, researchers obtained data captured just 47 days later by NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope. They also had follow-up observations from other ground- and space-based instruments, as well as data from roughly the past 30 years, which revealed the big star had started brightening in 2018.

Using all that data, the team was able to “reconstruct what happened with quite significant confidence,” Sven Buder, an astrophysicist at the Australian National University who did not participate in the study, tells the Australian Broadcasting Corporation’s Jacinta Bowler.

Computer simulations hinted that the two stars had orbited each other for millennia. Before the eye-catching explosion, the primary star—dubbed “Big Bao” after the eruption’s name—had become enormous. It was seven times more massive, 350 times the radius and 18,000 times brighter than our sun. Its companion, “Little Bao,” on the other hand, probably contained 0.7 times the mass of our sun and was smaller and fainter.

The smaller star spiraled into the bigger one’s envelope, and the two objects took about seven years to unite, which is quite quick in astronomical terms. The merger occurred when the red giant dragged its companion into its core, resulting in a dramatic event resembling “a bomb exploding inside a living star,” study co-author Kishalay De, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, says in a statement.

“We were able to see all different phases of this process—we were able to see the quiescent system, we were able to see the moment the stars touched each other, we were able to see the inspiral, and we were able to see the big outburst in 2025,” lead author Viraj Karambelkar, also an astrophysicist at Columbia University, tells New Scientist’s Leah Crane. “So we now know how this process works far better than we ever had before.”

Now, however, the system is too dusty for scientists to observe the aftermath directly, and it will likely remain so for years, reports Science News’ Meghan Bartels. In the meantime, Karambelkar says they can work to “catch more of these systems even before they erupt.”

articles.title: Rembrandt's 'Night Watch' Is Teeming With Life. Researchers Reveal a Hidden World of Microbes All Over the Masterpiece

paras.en: For nearly four centuries, viewers have admired the bustling militia figures frozen in oil paint on Rembrandt van Rijn’s 1642 masterpiece, The Night Watch. Now, scientists in Amsterdam have revealed that the iconic canvas is teeming with an invisible, living world of its own.

Researchers from the Rijksmuseum and ARTIS-Micropia (which claims to be the world’s only museum dedicated to microbes) are collecting 60 samples from 10 different areas of the painting to catalog its surface microbiome. Early laboratory cultures have turned up myriads of common bacteria and one puzzling outlier: Microbacterium saccharophilum, a bacterial species first identified in 2013 at a sugar refinery in Japan.

“This is the first time The Night Watch, or any work of art, has been analyzed in this way, and we’ve found bacteria that appear on human skin and in soil, and are even associated with plants,” Eline van Bloois, a microbiologist at Artis-Micropia tells El País’ Isabel Ferrer.

The ongoing investigation is featured in “The Night Watch Lives,” an exhibition at ARTIS-Micropia running through May 2027. Centered around a life-size reproduction of Rembrandt’s painting marked with numbered sampling dates, the display showcases living bacterial colonies growing inside glass-encased Petri dishes.
“To get that close to the painting was very scary,” van Bloois tells Hyperallergic's Noëlle de Leeuw. “After all, it's a piece of art that is so well-known to so many people.”

The microbial census forms a new chapter of “Operation Night Watch,” the Rijksmuseum’s sweeping research and conservation initiative launched in 2019. Inside a glass chamber in the museum’s Gallery of Honor, conservators are currently working in full view of visitors to painstakingly remove a yellowed layer of varnish applied in the 1970s. It’s a delicate process, using organic-fabric gauze, small tissues and tiny amounts of solvent that will take years to complete.

Decades before Dutch microbiologist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first described microorganisms in the 1670s, Rembrandt was already using chemistry to protect his work against microscopic threats. Previous Operation Night Watch analyses revealed that Rembrandt had applied a layer of lead-laden oil beneath the primer to shield the painting from moisture and mold in Amsterdam’s damp buildings. The canvas was later trimmed in 1715 to fit inside Amsterdam City Hall and has suffered numerous conservation treatments and deep cleanings roughly once every 50 years.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Since 2019, Operation Night Watch has made several other breakthroughs. Researchers restored the trimmed edges of the painting with artificial intelligence and discovered a hidden sketch beneath the paint with advanced X-ray imaging.

“Thirty or 40 years ago, nobody could have imagined you’d be talking to a chemist or biologist about The Night Watch,” Rijksmuseum director Taco Dibbits said during a press conference, Hyperallergic reports. “And I think precisely because this research is broadening—the fact that the humanities and the exact sciences are collaborating—it also leads to it becoming more widely embraced.”

To sample the 400-year-old surface safely, conservators and lab technicians gently pressed small, sterile cellulose discs against both varnished and unvarnished sections of the canvas. Those discs were transferred to Petri dishes and incubated in ARTIS-Micropia’s laboratory until invisible microbes multiplied into visible colonies, which an external lab then identified.

The team has completed only half of its six planned sampling trips to the Rijksmuseum so far, with 20 identified microbes currently on display and another 10 still incubating. Researchers expect to collect all 60 samples by February.

Among the familiar microbial residents detected so far are Staphylococcus epidermidis and Micrococcus luteus, harmless bacteria routinely found on human skin that help hydrate it and defend against pathogens, Amsterdamian’s Dana Marin reports. The team also isolated plant-root and soil species, including Kocuria palustris, Kocuria rhizophila and Lysinibacillus sphaericus, a resilient bacterium capable of surviving harsh environments rich in heavy metals.

None of those, however, baffled scientists quite like Microbacterium saccharophilum, which turned up on a section where old varnish had already been stripped away. Originally isolated from soil at the Ensuiko Sugar Refining plant in Yokohama, Japan, the microbe has no obvious connection to a Dutch Golden Age canvas.

“We’ve seen very little sugar in Rembrandt’s painting so far, and it’s best not to speculate, but it’s possible that the Saccharophilum isn’t as old as the canvas,” van Bloois tells El País, adding that scientists currently have no way to determine when any of the bacteria arrived.

Museum visitors often wonder whether any microbes lingering on the paint might date back to Rembrandt himself. “Ideally, you want to have the bacteria of Rembrandt: this is the Holy Grail,” Katrien Keune, the Rijksmuseum’s head of science, tells the Art Newspaper’s Senay Boztas. Yet Keune tells Amsterdamian that centuries of restoration make finding traces of the master unlikely, noting that the surface largely reflects museum staff and visitors shedding skin cells and saliva droplets.

Even without a direct biological link to Rembrandt, researchers hope the project helps rehabilitate the public image of microbes, pointing out that far less than 1 percent of known species cause disease in humans or animals. “It's good to give microbes some love as well,” van Bloois tells the Art Newspaper.
“The Night Watch Lives” is on view at ARTIS-Micropia in Amsterdam through May 2027.

articles.title: A Roman Cup and Hundreds of Other Treasures Unearthed in This 2,000-Year-Old Tomb Reveal the Rich Exchange Network of an Ancient Asian Empire

paras.en: Some 2,000 years ago, an elite individual associated with the nomadic Xiongnu Empire was buried in style in what is now northeastern Mongolia. Their tomb, measuring nearly 240 feet in length (about four-fifths the height of the Statue of Liberty), is the largest of its kind discovered in the East Asian country to date.

Despite this impressive exterior, the tomb’s interior is surprisingly small and shallow. But it was packed with treasures that shed new light on the Xiongnu people’s links to such far-flung foreign powers as the Roman Empire and the Lelang Commandery, an administrative division of China’s Han dynasty that was based in what is now Korea.

The National Museum of Korea, the Institute of Archaeology at the Mongolian Academy of Sciences and the National Museum of Mongolia recently completed a four-year excavation of the burial, which is known officially as Tomb 160. It’s located in Duurlig Nars, a Xiongnu burial ground with some 300 graves.
- UNESCO added the Duurlig Nars complex to its World Heritage List earlier this year.
- The United Nations agency recognized the site’s tombs for highlighting “the engineering and organizational skills of this predominantly nomadic culture.”

Archaeologists recovered 413 artifacts from the tomb, including a glass cup believed to be of Roman origin, a gourd-shaped silver pendant that once adorned a horse’s harness, a lacquered chariot and 15 jade pieces modeled after Han funerary goods.

The pendant resembles accessories found in Lelang tombs in modern-day North Korea, but unlike those ornaments, it boasts a crystal at its center. The jade objects, meanwhile, were fashioned in irregular shapes with intricate designs carved onto their surfaces, setting them apart from the disc-shaped bi prized by the Han as symbols of heaven.

“This excavation clearly shows that the Xiongnu of 2,000 years ago were linked to a broad exchange network reaching from Rome to the Korean Peninsula,” the National Museum of Korea says in a statement, per a translation by Seoul Economic Daily. “We expect it to serve as a turning point in expanding the field of Korean archaeology into Eurasia.”

The rich range of objects buried alongside the deceased testifies to their high status. Although the researchers have yet to identify the grave’s occupant, they plan to conduct a DNA analysis of teeth and hair recovered from the individual’s coffin to determine their sex and age.

To construct the tomb, ancient laborers built an elevated terrace enclosed by nine layers of stacked stones. The central chamber of the grave extends to a depth of nearly 50 feet, making it significantly smaller than comparable Xiongnu tombs in central Mongolia, whose depths reach more than 70 feet. The excavation team suggests that this downsized interior reflects societal shifts in the late first and second centuries C.E., when the tomb was built. At the time, the Xiongnu Empire was declining, with internal disagreements and external pressure from the Han military weakening the once-great pastoral confederation.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The Xiongnu thrived in Central Asia between the third century B.C.E. and the second century C.E., wielding control over vast swaths of territory “without building cities, forming central bureaucracies, devising a writing system or mobilizing masses of farmers to produce food,” Bruce Bower wrote for Science News in 2023. In recent years, scholars have revealed an array of insights on the Xiongnu that challenge long-held perceptions of the group as “barbaric” invaders.

In 2023, for example, a paper published in the journal Science Advances suggested that elite Xiongnu women traveled to the empire’s frontiers to shore up alliances with powerful locals. “They are representatives of the imperial clan that ruled the empire,” study co-author Bryan Miller, an archaeologist at the University of Michigan, told Live Science’s Tom Metcalfe. “You’ve got these marriage alliances spanning the whole empire, even in these local communities.”
Speaking with Science News, Miller added, “This must have been an empire organized around moving populations. Xiongnu elites were savvy politicians who delegated power to keep the empire together.”

articles.title: Internet Archive Staffers Are Unionizing
articles.author: Caroline Haskins

paras.en: Staffers at the Internet Archive, the nonprofit “digital library” that runs the Wayback Machine, are voting to join the Communications Workers of America (CWA).

More than 80 of the 124 eligible US staffers voted in favor of unionizing, and they are currently awaiting voluntary recognition of the union from Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle. Kahle did not immediately respond to WIRED’s request for comment. If Kahle does not grant voluntary recognition, employees will vote whether to certify the union in a process run by the National Labor Relations Board.

The Internet Archive, which also offers free catalogs preserving tens of millions of digital and physical media items, was founded by Kahle in 1996. Kahle’s mission was to provide “Universal Access to All Knowledge.” Will Howes, an Internet Archive engineer, says that the organizing process has demonstrated how “aligned” employees are in their passion for Kahle’s goals.

“Frankly, we really see the formation of this union as accepting [Kahle’s] challenge to make this workplace the best place it can be in pursuit of a mission, universal access to all knowledge,” Howes tells WIRED.

Microfiche digitization technician Danielle Leard tells WIRED that the union is “very optimistic” that Kahle will voluntarily recognize it and come to the bargaining table. They add that among the union’s core goals are securing wage increases and additional benefits, and ensuring that these benefits are consistently available to employees across the company.

“We believe the first and most primary goal of our union is to make sure that the Internet Archive reflects the wants and values of the people that work there, and the people that make the archive,” Leard says.

Howes and Leard tell WIRED that the Internet Archive—which claims to have archived more than 1 trillion web pages—employs a highly diverse set of workers, including librarians, engineers, physical media specialists, and facility coordinators who maintain the archive’s building, a former Christian Scientist church in San Francisco. Leard says that the staff’s diversity has made the organizing process, which began in February 2025, “a unique challenge,” but one that’s “really rewarding.”

The vote comes slightly more than two months after staffers at the Wikimedia Foundation, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia, voted to join CWA. Howes says the simultaneous efforts are “very powerful” given that both organizations represent “core infrastructure” of the internet.

Howes says that the union wants to ensure that the 30-year-old project continues to thrive in the long term—and that its workers do too. Leard says this means providing paths for developing skills and getting promoted within the nonprofit.
Leard says that the Internet Archive’s unionization drive is especially important in the present moment, amid waves of tech layoffs and widespread anxiety about “emerging technologies” like AI.

The Internet Archive hasn’t been immune from the consequences of AI. A Nieman Lab report from January found that some news websites, struggling to prevent companies like OpenAI or Anthropic from harvesting their articles, have started blocking web crawlers from the Internet Archive, arguing it gives AI companies a back door to their content. (The archive relies on web crawlers to preserve news articles in near-real time.)
Leard says that ideally, the Internet Archive’s unionization will be “one domino” in a larger process that makes the tech industry better.
“We're hoping,” they say, “that we'll continue to be one of the blueprints that will make it easier for other organizations and companies in the future to continue to unionize.”

Update: 11/20/26 1:43pm ET: This story has been updated to reflect that Internet Archive workers have voted in favor of unionizing, but the union has not yet been recognized by Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle.

articles.title: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation
articles.author: Lauren Goode, Paresh Dave

paras.en: Jensen Huang was ousted from Nvidia amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Yet it was “multiple issues” related to Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying” that ultimately moved the board of directors, according to two people familiar with private discussions among the chair and other members.

While Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang on November 8, the board couldn’t determine in the moment whether she was an intelligence operative for China, these sources say. That same day, the board announced an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting” that their CEO had “been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has rejected allegations that Alice Huang was a spy.

But in the following days, once allegations of other affairs surfaced, including one reportedly with a direct report, “what could be determined was [Huang’s] lying, and that spanned a year, from October 2025 through recent events,” a source close to the board told WIRED, who requested anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak on its behalf.

According to sources, members of the board had asked Huang about Alice Huang after The New York Times first reported in October 2025 that Nvidia had an unusually robust business relationship with a Singapore-based data center company named Megaspeed, where Alice Huang worked. Jensen Huang at the time denied any inappropriate relationship with Alice Huang to the board, sources tell WIRED.

After the affair came to light, the board was incensed, these people say. A source familiar with the board’s thinking told WIRED that while these board members view issues of national security as “important” and “ongoing,” the primary driver behind Huang’s ouster was “the lying.”
“It was a matter of integrity and trust,” this person said.

In recent days, board members, including chair Harvey Jones, have tried to quell the discourse about Huang’s possible return to Nvidia by emphasizing that Huang's behavior flew in the face of Nvidia’s policies and corporate governance rules, sources tell WIRED. While previous reporting by WIRED and other news outlets have outlined factors that Jones has said played into the board’s decision, the primary motivation hadn’t been previously specified.

Board chair Harvey Jones did not respond to a WIRED request for comment. A spokesperson for Nvidia, John Rizzo, declined to comment. John Fisher, vice president at the communications firm Trident, which is representing Huang, declined to comment except to say that Huang voluntarily resigned from his positions at Nvidia.

For Nvidia’s board, the possibility that Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government poses a bigger problem than an executive’s personal misconduct. If she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, the scandal isn’t just about Huang’s alleged “lack of candor,” but a potential security and governance crisis.

Already the scandal has given China hawks grist to call for tighter controls on US business dealings with China. In addition, multiple government agencies and offices have called for investigations into what the former Nvidia CEO may have known about the company’s chips getting into China. The company’s general counsel Tim Teter has also been called to Washington, DC to testify, as government officials try to find out more about Nvidia’s possible flouting of export controls.

Nvidia and Huang are also facing several shareholder lawsuits, alleging the CEO and the company made misleading statements about dealings with Alice Huang and Megaspeed. Other Silicon Valley investors have publicly raised concerns about insufficient corporate governance and executive oversight by the board.

In the company’s all-hands meeting on November 18, board chair Jones said it was “not an easy decision to accept [Huang’s] resignation,” according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. “However, the disclosure of personal behavior and a lack of candor inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and values made this a necessary decision.”

Meanwhile, fans and supporters of Huang, including thousands of Nvidia employees and Elon Musk, have continued to call for his return to Nvidia. Huang himself has said he would be “honored” to come back as CEO. On Friday, US President Donald Trump renewed his call for Huang to have another chance. “He made some bad decisions, but he is a brilliant person,” Trump told reporters. “I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology.”

The news outlet Semafor reported that a small faction of Nvidia’s board of directors has pushed to bring Huang back as well. Jones has not responded to WIRED’s inquiries about the board’s reported division on the topic of Huang’s return.

Some employees are miffed at how quickly the board accepted Huang’s resignation, insisting the longtime leader must have been the victim of a coordinated campaign intended to unseat him. “We feel like they forced his hands to resign,” says one person on the business side at Nvidia. “We don’t understand why the board is so adamant about not giving him a second chance.”

At the all-hands meeting, interim CEO Colette Kress said employees’ biggest concern was Nvidia’s falling share price. The next biggest concern was the board’s decision to oust Huang. But while she addressed the first by moving up pay raises, she offered no promise on sharing results of the board’s investigation into Huang or its deliberations about him.
“The ship has sinked but there’s no plan to be transparent about what happened,” says one computer scientist working at Nvidia. “It feels like a black box.”

articles.title: Boosie Badazz Charge Over Alleged Nightclub Assault Dismissed — But His Legal Troubles Aren’t Over
articles.author: Rachel Scharf

paras.en: Boosie Badazz has defeated a felony case over an alleged violent altercation at a Houston nightclub this year — though the rapper’s legal troubles are not yet over.

The Louisiana rapper (Torrence Hatch) was arrested in May for aggravated assault after being accused of smashing a club bouncer in the head with a glass hookah. But court records reviewed by Billboard show that the case was dismissed on Friday (Nov. 20) after a grand jury in Houston did not find enough evidence to bring formal charges.

Boosie’s lawyer, Kent Schaffer, told Billboard on Friday, “We have said from the beginning that this was an attempt to get money from Boosie, and we feel vindicated that the grand jury found there was no probable cause for an indictment.”

“The grand jury was presented with affidavits from eyewitnesses that were in attendance that night,” added Schaffer. “Conversely, the state had no evidence other than from the complainant whose credibility was horrible, at best.”
A rep for the Harris County District Attorney’s Office did not immediately return a request for comment.

Though the criminal assault case is now behind him, Boosie is still fighting a civil lawsuit over the alleged May incident at Houston’s Dome nightclub. Bouncer Edward Iglehart claims the rapper “violently attacked him” with a hookah and is seeking more than $5 million in damages from both the rapper and the club.
Boosie vehemently denies Iglehart’s claim, and Schaffer told Billboard on Friday, “The civil case is still pending but probably not for much longer.”

Meanwhile, Boosie also faces another criminal case in federal court for illegally owning a gun despite prior felony convictions. He received a no-jail sentence after pleading guilty to the charge last year, but probation supervisors recently asked the judge to reconsider sending him to prison.

The U.S. Probation Office flagged in June that Boosie had violated the terms of his supervised release by committing another crime via the Houston club incident. That will likely be moot now that the charge has been dismissed, though probation officers also claimed he broke the rules by using marijuana and crossing state lines without permission.

Boosie has vehemently denied those accusations, writing on X in June that he’s “doing great on federal probation” and “crystal clean” of all drugs. “IM NOT STUPID,” the rapper told his followers on social media. He’s scheduled to appear in federal court for a status update in January.

Amid all of that, Boosie is also pursuing his own legal action against a pair of lobbyists who supposedly promised they could get him pardoned by President Donald Trump for a $600,000 fee. Boosie says this was bogus and wants a $300,000 refund.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘Stupid Song’ Hits No. 1 on Billboard’s Pop Airplay Chart
articles.author: Gary Trust

paras.en: Having become a spark in the dark, and all dayparts, Olivia Rodrigo’s “Stupid Song” reaches the top spot on Billboard’s Pop Airplay chart (dated Nov. 28), jumping three places to No. 1.

Rodrigo earns her fourth leader at the format and her second from her third studio album, you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, following the set’s lead single, “Drop Dead,” for a week in August. She notched her first two No. 1s from her debut LP, Sour, in 2021: “Drivers License,” for five weeks beginning that March and “Good 4 U,” for six weeks starting that July.

Rodrigo is also scaling Pop Airplay with “Expectations,” with Chappell Roan, up to a new No. 20 high. (The song was originally released on you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, while its duet remix arrived Oct. 16.) Plus, “The Cure,” additionally from the set, is drawing play among the chart’s reporters, along with her new carol, “Take Me Home (4 Christmas).”
Pop Airplay ranks the most-played titles on nearly 150 U.S. mainstream top 40 stations, as monitored by Mediabase (which provides airplay data to Luminate for Billboard’s radio rankings).

You seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, released on Geffen/Interscope Capitol, premiered at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in June and has led the list for five weeks running, tying Sour for her longest command.
As announced Monday (Nov. 16), Rodrigo scored seven Grammy nominations via you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, including album of the year, with the 2027 awards ceremony set for Feb. 7.
All charts dated Nov. 28 will update on Billboard.com Tuesday, Nov. 24.

articles.title: Emmy Rossum on Producing and Starring in ‘Furious’: “I Have Been ‘Matrix’-Style Dodging Mega-Predators Since I Was Seven”
articles.author: Scott Feinberg

paras.en: “I have been Matrix-style dodging mega-predators since I was seven years old,” actress-producer Emmy Rossum said during a recording of The Hollywood Reporter’s Awards Chatter podcast at the recent Newport Beach Film Festival, where she was being honored with the fest’s Outstanding Performance in Television Award for her work on Hulu’s Furious. The drama series, which she also produced, tells a cat-and-mouse tale of a female FBI agent (Rossum) and a young female serial killer (Lola Petticrew), both PTSD-afflicted survivors of sexual abuse. “So,” Rossum continued, “I firsthand understand the nuance and complexity of being a young person in situations like this and of being a powerful professional woman in situations like this.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Rossum, who was once described by the late Roger Ebert as “a phenomenal talent,” is only 40, but she has been doing outstanding work for nearly 30 years — in films like 2000s Songcatcher, 2003’s Mystic River, 2004’s The Phantom of the Opera and 2013’s Beautiful Creatures; TV limited series such as Angelyne (2022) and The Crowded Room (2023); and, of course, for 110 episodes over nine seasons on the TV series Shameless (2011-2019), several episodes of which she also directed.
paras.zh: 已故影评人罗杰·埃伯特（Roger Ebert）曾将罗森形容为“天才横溢”。她今年只有40岁，但已经有近30年的出色演艺生涯——包括2000年的《追寻民谣》（Songcatcher）、2003年的《神秘河流》（Mystic River）、2004年的《歌剧魅影》（The Phantom of the Opera）和2013年的《美丽生灵》（Beautiful Creatures）等电影；《安吉琳》（Angelyne，2022年）和《拥挤的房间》（The Crowded Room，2023年）等限定剧集；当然还有电视剧《无耻之徒》（Shameless，2011-2019年）的九季110集，其中几集她还担任了导演。

paras.en: As Rossum’s time on Shameless came to an end, she launched a production company, Composition 8, which she now runs with her husband, Mr. Robot creator Sam Esmail, and a development executive, Sara Moskowitz. Their first project was Angelyne, in which Rossum played the eponymous Los Angeles billboard queen. They have since made several others. Rossum explains, “The throughline in things that I’ve been looking for is: I like characters that are living in moral gray areas. That’s something that I wasn’t really able to do in the ingenue years.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: But obtaining choice material is not easy for a small company, even one run by a top young actress. “We have to be scrappy because we’re not LuckyChap [Margot Robbie’s company], and we’re not Hello Sunshine [Reese Witherspoon’s company],” she explains. “We’re three people with this mandate of wanting to tell complicated stories about women that talk about something in the zeitgeist and culture and where we are now — and make really entertaining and fun stuff.”
paras.zh: 但对于一家小公司来说，获得优质的素材并不容易，即使这家公司是由一位顶级年轻女演员经营的。“我们必须奋力拼搏，因为我们不是LuckyChap [玛格特·罗比的公司]，也不是Hello Sunshine [瑞茜·威瑟斯彭的公司]，”她解释道。“我们三个人肩负着这样的使命：想要讲述关于女性的复杂故事，这些故事要反映时代精神、文化以及我们当下的处境——同时还要创作真正有娱乐性、有意思的作品。”

paras.en: What led them to Furious, their most successful project yet? Rossum recounts, “I was like, ‘OK, well, we’re not going to land any of the hot books, so where do we go look? We have to look where other people are not looking. Let’s look at all of the old movies that nobody’s looking at. Like, they were good, so why aren’t we looking there? There’s got to be one that’s got a good skeleton that we can uncover and figure it out.'”
paras.zh: 是什么让他们接下了迄今为止最成功的项目《速度与激情》？Rossum回忆道：“我当时想，‘好吧，我们拿不到任何热门剧本，那我们该去哪里找呢？我们必须关注别人没有关注的地方。让我们来看看所有没人看的旧电影。这些电影都很好，那我们为什么不去看看呢？其中一定有一部有好的骨架，我们可以发掘出来，搞清楚它。”

paras.en: That led them to Bob Rafelson’s 1987 cult classic Black Widow, which starred Debra Winger and Theresa Russell as an FBI agent and serial killer, respectively. The material was nearly 40 years old, but still “feels kind of contemporary,” she felt, noting eerie parallels with everything from the Jeffrey Epstein saga to the “Jane Doe” case at Cornell. So Composition 8 obtained the rights and set about putting it together. Rossum sold the show to Hulu via a text, recruited Liz Meriwether (The Dropout) to serve as showrunner and set about preparing to play cop-turned-FBI agent Alice Black, meeting with and shadowing law enforcement officials, consulting psychotherapists, adding considerable muscle to her small physique and more.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: She reflects, “It’s interesting to play a character who can hold so many complexities, who can be infinitely, bottomlessly vulnerable and terrified and afraid to be weak at the same time as being incredibly manipulative and physically and emotionally powerful and dogged and smart and underestimated. It was the role that haunted me the most, and it was a benefit that I came on so early, because I felt that I was working on the character for three years before we started shooting.”
paras.zh: 她感慨道：“扮演一个如此复杂多面的角色很有意思。她既能表现出无限的、深不见底的脆弱、恐惧和害怕软弱，又能表现出极强的操控性、身心上的强大、顽强、聪明和被低估。这个角色最让我念念不忘，我这么早加入剧组是一件好事，因为我觉得在开拍之前，我已经为这个角色琢磨了三年。”

paras.en: The first season of Furious, which rolled out in July and August, was described by The New York Times as “remarkable.” Rossum’s part, meanwhile, was described by The Guardian as “the role of her life.” For it, she is now in serious contention for end-of-the-year honors — best actress in a drama series Critics Choice, Golden Globe and Actor Awards — and, next year, she might well become the first person with the name Emmy to, well, win one.
paras.zh: 《Furious》第一季于7月和8月播出，《纽约时报》将其评价为“出色”。与此同时，《卫报》将罗森的角色描述为“她一生中最重要的角色”。凭借这一角色，她目前正在激烈角逐年末的各项荣誉——评论家选择奖、金球奖和演员奖的剧情类剧集最佳女主角奖。明年，她很可能会成为第一个名叫艾美的人，呃，赢得艾美奖。

paras.en: In the meantime, though, she’s headed back to work: a second season of Furious was ordered just before its season one finale aired, and it starts shooting in January. She can’t wait — but she also wants the industry to know that she’s not only interested in acting in stuff that she also produces: “I’m still in the incoming-call business, so please hire me! I want great roles.”
paras.zh: 不过与此同时，她已经准备好重返工作岗位：《怒火》第一季大结局播出前，第二季就已获得续订，并将于1月开拍。她迫不及待地想开始工作，但她也希望业内人士知道，她不仅有兴趣出演自己也参与制作的作品：“我仍然在等待机会，所以请聘用我！我想要出色的角色。”

articles.title: “The Secrecy Was Insane:” The Making of ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,’ From Locked Safes to Original Cast’s Return
articles.author: Lexy Perez

paras.en: Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it.
paras.zh: 有些故事拒绝留在页面上。 《好莱坞报道》的《超越书本》专栏探讨了当书籍跃上银幕及其他领域时会发生什么——揭开哪些内容留下来、哪些内容发生了变化、它是如何完成的，以及为什么它对制作它的创意人员来说很重要。

paras.en: Before the odds could be in their favor, the creative team behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping had to survive a Games of their own, one played entirely in secret.
paras.zh: 在胜算对他们有利之前，《饥饿游戏：收割日出》背后的创意团队必须在一场完全秘密进行的游戏中生存下来。

paras.en: The rules were simple: one copy of the book, no internet and not a word to anyone.
paras.zh: 规则很简单：一本书，不能上网，不能对任何人说一句话。

paras.en: When Hunger Games author Suzanne Collins called her trusted adapters, director Francis Lawrence, producer Nina Jacobson and original Hunger Games screenwriter Billy Ray, they were eager to read her new story. The catch: it wasn’t fully finished, and it hadn’t been announced to the public. That meant caution was essential.
paras.zh: 当《饥饿游戏》的作者苏珊娜·柯林斯给她信任的改编者、导演弗朗西斯·劳伦斯、制片人尼娜·雅各布森和《饥饿游戏》原编剧比利·雷打电话时，他们都渴望阅读她的新故事。问题是：它还没有完全完成，也没有向公众宣布。这意味着谨慎是至关重要的。

paras.en: Take Ray’s process for example. The screenwriter didn’t write his latest Hunger Games script on his own computer. Each day, he drove onto the Fox lot to Jacobson’s office and sat down in a small room with a safe that guarded Collins’ story. An assistant opened the safe, took out a laptop that had never been connected to the internet and set it in front of him. He wrote all day, said “Done,” and the laptop went back into the safe.
paras.zh: 以Ray的流程为例。编剧并没有在自己的电脑上编写最新的《饥饿游戏》剧本。每天，他都会开车到福克斯停车场去雅各布森的办公室，坐在一间小房间里，里面有一个保险箱，用来保管柯林斯的故事。助理打开保险箱，拿出一台从未联网的笔记本电脑放在他面前。他写了一整天，说“完成”，然后笔记本电脑就放回了保险箱。

paras.en: “That’s how the script got written, which of course I had never done before,” Ray tells The Hollywood Reporter.
paras.zh: “剧本就是这样写的，当然我以前从未这样做过，”雷告诉《好莱坞报道》。

paras.en: It was an unusual way to adapt a novel that almost no one outside that small circle knew existed, yet maintaining strict confidentiality was imperative given the phenomenon Collins’ franchise has become. The original four films — The Hunger Games, Catching Fire and Mockingjay Part 1 and 2 — grossed roughly $2.98 billion worldwide. Debuting with its first book in 2008, the dystopian saga following teenagers forced into fatal combat has grown into one of the most successful young adult publishing franchises in history. Across its five installments, the series has sold more than 100 million copies globally.
paras.zh: 这是一种不寻常的改编小说的方式，在这个小圈子之外几乎没有人知道它的存在，但考虑到柯林斯的特许经营已经成为一种现象，严格保密是必要的。最初的四部电影——《饥饿游戏》、《星火燎原》和《嘲笑鸟》第 1 部和第 2 部——全球票房收入约为 29.8 亿美元。这部讲述青少年被迫陷入致命战斗的反乌托邦传奇故事于 2008 年推出第一本书，现已发展成为历史上最成功的青少年出版系列之一。该系列共五部，全球销量已超过 1 亿份。

paras.en: In 2020, Collins released her first prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, which chronicled the rise of the tyrant Coriolanus Snow. The film was adapted for feature film starring Tom Blyth and Rachel Zegler. Now with Sunrise on the Reaping, released on Nov. 20, Collins has returned to another familiar face: Haymitch Abernathy, the District 12 mentor Woody Harrelson played in the films.
paras.zh: 2020 年，柯林斯发布了她的第一部前传《鸣禽与蛇之歌》，该书记录了暴君科利奥兰纳斯·斯诺的崛起。该影片被改编为故事片，由汤姆·布莱思和瑞秋·齐格勒主演。现在，随着 11 月 20 日上映的《收割日出》，柯林斯又回归了另一位熟悉的面孔：黑密斯·阿伯内西，他是电影中第 12 区导师伍迪·哈里森的扮演者。

paras.en: The prequel revisits the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, when a younger Haymitch (portrayed by Joseph Zada) competes. Sunrise on the Reaping opens on Haymitch’s 16th birthday, which coincides with the second Quarter Quell, where the traditional choice of one male and one female from a district has been doubled to two of each.
paras.zh: 前传重温了《饥饿游戏》事件发生 24 年前的施惠国世界，从第 50 届饥饿游戏（也称为第二季度镇压）结束的早晨开始，年轻的黑密斯（由约瑟夫·扎达饰演）参加了比赛。 《收割日出》在黑密斯 16 岁生日那天开幕，恰逢第二季度镇压，传统上从一个地区选择一名男性和一名女性的做法已增加了一倍，达到每人两名。

paras.en: Though initially not among the four selected tributes for District 12, Haymitch is automatically volunteered as punishment for trying to protect his girlfriend Lenore (Whitney Peak) who reacts after one of the chosen boys tries to make a run for it and is shot by Capitol soldiers known as “Peacekeepers.”
paras.zh: 虽然黑密斯一开始并未被列入第 12 区的四名致敬对象中，但黑密斯却自动自愿加入，作为对试图保护女友莱诺尔（惠特尼·皮克饰）的惩罚。其中一名被选中的男孩试图逃跑，莱诺尔做出反应，被被称为“和平卫士”的国会大厦士兵开枪射杀。

paras.en: The Haymitch origin story answers a question fans have had since the first film: how the hopeful, mischievous kid became the bitter, drunken mentor to Jennifer Lawrence‘s Katniss Everdeen and Josh Hutcherson‘s Peeta Mellark that Harrelson played.
paras.zh: 黑密斯的起源故事回答了影迷自第一部电影以来一直存在的一个问题：这个充满希望、顽皮的孩子如何成为詹妮弗·劳伦斯饰演的凯特尼斯·伊夫丁和乔什·哈切森饰演的哈里森扮演的皮塔·梅拉克的苦涩、醉酒的导师。

paras.en: Ahead of the film’s release, Ray, Jacobson and director Francis Lawrence spoke with THR about working under an NDA bubble, finding their new Haymitch and reuniting franchise alums Harrelson, Lawrence and Hutcherson.
paras.zh: 在电影上映前，雷、雅各布森和导演弗​​朗西斯·劳伦斯接受了《好莱坞报道》采访，谈论了在保密协议泡沫下工作、寻找新的黑密斯以及将特许经营权的成员哈里森、劳伦斯和哈切森重聚的事情。

paras.en: When The Hunger Games was first adapted for the screen, screenwriter Ray and director Gary Ross launched what would grow into a global success. Since both Ray and Ross parted ways with the franchise following the initial installment, Ray’s comeback to craft the backstory for a character he helped popularize represented a complete full-circle experience.
paras.zh: 当《饥饿游戏》首次被搬上银幕时，编剧雷和导演加里·罗斯推出了一部后来在全球取得成功的作品。由于雷和罗斯在第一部作品后就与该系列分道扬镳，雷的回归为他帮助普及的角色制作背景故事代表了一次完整的全循环体验。

paras.en: “Having launched that franchise, The Hunger Games has been such a blessing in my career,” Ray tells THR. “I can’t begin to enumerate all the ways it’s been great for me.”
paras.zh: “推出该系列后，《饥饿游戏》对我的职业生涯来说是一件幸事，”雷告诉《好莱坞报道》。 “我无法一一列举它对我的所有好处。”

paras.en: “When the opportunity came to come back, I said yes before I read the book,” he says of his return. “It was something I wanted to do. I wanted to work with Francis, and I wanted to be back under the hood with Suzanne and with Nina.”
paras.zh: “当有机会回来时，我在读这本书之前就答应了，”他谈到自己的回归时说道。 “这是我想做的事情。我想和弗朗西斯一起工作，我想回到幕后与苏珊娜和尼娜一起工作。”

paras.en: Ray has stayed close with Collins, who read an early draft of his debut novel, Burn the Water, which was released earlier this year. “It was as if we had spoken the day before,” he says of reteaming with Collins and others for Sunrise on the Reaping. “There was just no falloff at all.”
paras.zh: 雷与柯林斯关系密切，柯林斯阅读了他今年早些时候发行的处女作《烧水》的初稿。 “就好像我们前一天就已经说过话一样，”他在谈到与柯林斯和其他人重新合作《收割日出》时说道。 “根本没有任何衰减。”

paras.en: When Collins calls, producer Jacobson, director Lawrence and Ray answer, ready to find out what the author has created this time. But her first question is always the same: “Why don’t you guys take a look and let me know if you think it’s a movie?”
paras.zh: 当柯林斯打来电话时，制片人雅各布森、导演劳伦斯和雷接听，准备看看作者这次创作了什么。但她的第一个问题总是一样的：“你们为什么不看看，如果你们认为这是一部电影，请告诉我？”

paras.en: “This is always kind of hilarious… We read this one and said, ‘Yeah, it’s a movie, Suzanne,'” Lawrence says, laughing. Jacobson’s answer was just as immediate: “My first response was, ‘Hell yes.'”
paras.zh: “这总是有点搞笑……我们读了这篇文章后说，‘是的，这是一部电影，苏珊娜，’”劳伦斯笑着说。雅各布森的回答同样直接：“我的第一反应是，‘当然是的。’”

paras.en: Collins’ question is a sincere one, though, Lawrence explains. “She’s very serious when she says it’s OK to tell her it’s not a movie. When you create anything, you’re vulnerable, and when she hands something to us, it’s usually not completely finished. She feels vulnerable about it and wants some reassurance that it really is worthy of being on the screen.”
paras.zh: 不过，劳伦斯解释说，柯林斯的问题是真诚的。 “当她说可以告诉她这不是一部电影时，她非常认真。当你创造任何东西时，你很脆弱，而当她把东西交给我们时，它通常还没有完全完成。她对此感到脆弱，并希望得到一些保证，确保它确实值得出现在屏幕上。”

paras.en: Getting that far took some doing. When the team read an early draft of The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, the world was in lockdown, so keeping it secret was easier, Lawrence says. Sunrise on the Reaping brought “a different kind of tension, because the book had not yet been published, so the secrecy and security around the project was pretty extreme,” Ray says.
paras.zh: 走到这一步需要付出一些努力。劳伦斯说，当团队阅读《鸟与蛇之歌》的早期草稿时，世界处于封锁状态，因此保守秘密更容易。雷说，《收割日出》带来了“一种不同的紧张气氛，因为这本书尚未出版，所以该项目的保密性和安全性非常严格”。

paras.en: “For us, the secrecy was insane,” Jacobson says. “We had one hard copy of the book. It had to be mailed or messengered from New York to L.A. in sections. First it lived at her [Collins’] agent’s house and then eventually we got a safe for my office and it moved into the safe. There was one copy, and people could make an appointment if they needed to read it.”
paras.zh: “对我们来说，保密是疯狂的，”雅各布森说。 “我们有这本书的一份硬拷贝。它必须从纽约邮寄或分批寄到洛杉矶。首先它住在她（柯林斯的）经纪人的家里，后来我们为我的办公室找到了一个保险箱，它搬进了保险箱。只有一份副本，人们如果需要阅读它可以预约。”

paras.en: The secrecy extended to casting, too. “Even once we had our script, we couldn’t release sides, or even use a scene from the book instead of sides, because if we read an actor, people would know what scenes and characters were in the book besides Haymitch,” Jacobson says. “So we had the young actors do improvs, just so we could get acquainted with this generation of actors and start to collect knowledge about who they are.”
paras.zh: 保密也延伸到了选角方面。 “即使我们有了剧本，我们也无法发布配角，甚至无法使用书中的场景来代替配角，因为如果我们读演员，人们就会知道书中除了黑密斯之外还有哪些场景和角色，”雅各布森说。 “所以我们让年轻演员进行即兴表演，这样我们就可以熟悉这一代演员并开始收集有关他们是谁的知识。”

paras.en: “Having to keep it locked down in this NDA bubble was exciting,” she adds. “It was sort of stressful, and I was incredibly relieved when we could finally talk about it!”
paras.zh: “必须将其锁定在 NDA 泡沫中是令人兴奋的，”她补充道。 “这有点压力，当我们终于可以谈论这件事时，我感到非常轻松！”

paras.en: “Interpretation, Not Impersonation”: Finding a New Haymitch
paras.zh: “解释，而不是模仿”：寻找新的黑密斯

paras.en: “We knew Haymitch was going to be the trickiest person to cast, because we’re anchored with him,” Lawrence says.
paras.zh: “我们知道黑密斯将是最难选角的人，因为我们以他为中心，”劳伦斯说。

paras.en: Joseph Zada, who starred in Prime Video’s We Were Liars and had filmed Netflix’s East of Eden series, caught the attention of casting directors Debra Zane and Dylan Jury, who wanted Lawrence and Jacobson to meet him.
paras.zh: 约瑟夫·扎达 (Joseph Zada) 曾出演 Prime Video 的《我们都是骗子》，并拍摄过 Netflix 的《伊甸之东》系列剧，引起了选角导演黛布拉·赞恩 (Debra Zane) 和迪伦·朱里 (Dylan Jury) 的注意，他们希望劳伦斯和雅各布森与他见面。

paras.en: “He had sent in an improv tape. We had many, many people do improv tapes just to see who was out in the world, and his was pretty special,” Lawrence recalls.
paras.zh: “他寄来了即兴录音带。我们有很多很多人制作即兴录音带，只是为了看看世界上有谁，而他的录音带非常特别，”劳伦斯回忆道。

paras.en: From there, the audition process became its own Hunger Games. “We really put him through the wringer in the audition process,” the director admits. “We tested and tested to make sure he would be emotionally capable of going through everything he needed to go through, that he had the sense of mischief and irreverence Woody has, and that he could embody all those characteristics without feeling like he was doing an impression. That was the tricky thing. But he was definitely the guy.”
paras.zh: 从那时起，试镜过程就变成了饥饿游戏。 “我们在试镜过程中确实让他经受了磨难，”导演承认。 “我们进行了一次又一次的测试，以确保他在情感上有能力经历他需要经历的一切，他有伍迪所具有的恶作剧和不敬感，并且他可以体现所有这些特征，而不会让人觉得他在给人留下深刻的印象。这是一件棘手的事情。但他绝对是那个人。”

paras.en: “We needed to know he had the range to experience all of the loss in the movie, and to do it in different ways: sometimes shame, guilt or anger, or just complete loss and grief,” Lawrence adds. “We needed somebody who could bring all of that.”
paras.zh: “我们需要知道他有能力经历电影中的所有损失，并以不同的方式做到这一点：有时是羞耻、内疚或愤怒，或者只是完全的损失和悲伤，”劳伦斯补充道。 “我们需要一个能够带来这一切的人。”

paras.en: For Jacobson, the deciding quality was mischief. “You needed somebody who had mischief in them, and that’s a surprisingly hard thing to find,” she says. “There are some wonderful, likable actors who are very capable leading men, but who don’t necessarily have that mischief in them, that troublemaker vibe. And yet at his young age, it can’t be that dark, twisted kind of mischief-maker or trickster. It’s a boyish quality.”
paras.zh: 对于雅各布森来说，决定性的品质是恶作剧。 “你需要一个有恶作剧的人，而这是一个出人意料的难找的人，”她说。 “有一些很棒、讨人喜欢的演员，他们是非常有能力的男主角，但他们身上不一定有那种恶作剧、麻烦制造者的氛围。但在他年轻的时候，不可能是那种黑暗、扭曲的恶作剧制造者或骗子。这是一种孩子气的品质。”

paras.en: Zada was someone who “had a hopeful, sunny disposition” and the mischief they wanted Haymitch to embody.
paras.zh: 扎达是一个“充满希望、阳光明媚的性格”的人，也是他们希望黑密斯体现的恶作剧。

paras.en: “When you first meet him in the original movies, you don’t understand why he’s so angry, drunken, broken and bitter. You assume, well, it can’t be easy being a mentor for the poorest, most disadvantaged district out there,” she continues. “What all of us wanted to see in this one, and what Joseph captured so beautifully, is that he was bright, funny, hopeful and very apolitical.”
paras.zh: “当你第一次在原版电影中见到他时，你不明白为什么他如此愤怒、醉酒、破碎和痛苦。你会想，嗯，成为最贫穷、最弱势地区的导师并不容易，”她继续道。 “我们所有人都想在这个人身上看到的，以及约瑟夫如此完美地捕捉到的，是他聪明、有趣、充满希望，而且非常不关心政治。”

paras.en: Zada’s chemistry with Peak, cast as his love interest, Lenore Dove, sealed it. “You just felt it. You felt like this woman is the woman he loves. She’s his best friend. She’s the person who makes it all make sense for him,” Jacobson says of their chemistry reads together.
paras.zh: 扎达与匹克（Peak）饰演他的爱人莱诺尔·多夫（Lenore Dove）之间的化学反应决定了这一点。 “你只是感觉到了。你觉得这个女人是他爱的女人。她是他最好的朋友。她是让这一切对他来说有意义的人，”雅各布森谈到他们一起阅读时的化学反应。

paras.en: “There’s a quality about Woody, and we had to find someone who had that quality but wasn’t going to get burdened by it,” she says. “With all of our actors, we always said, ‘We don’t want impersonation. We want interpretation.'”
paras.zh: “伍迪有一种品质，我们必须找到一个拥有这种品质但不会因此而受到负担的人，”她说。 “对于我们所有的演员，我们总是说，‘我们不想要模仿。我们想要诠释。’”

paras.en: That philosophy extended well beyond Haymitch. From Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning to Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons and Ralph Fiennes, Sunrise wasn’t short on A-listers joining its younger, newer cast members that also included Mckenna Grace, Ben Wang, Molly McCann and Percy Daggs IV.
paras.zh: 这种哲学远远超出了黑密斯的范围。从基兰·卡尔金、艾丽·范宁到格伦·克洛斯、杰西·普莱蒙和拉尔夫·费因斯，《日出》不乏一线明星加入其年轻、新的演员阵容，其中还包括麦肯娜·格蕾丝、本·王、莫莉·麦肯和珀西·达格斯四世。

paras.en: But joining an established franchise isn’t always an immediate yes, Jacobson says. “There are definitely some people who just don’t know the series that well, so it’s about educating them about it, and making sure they know we’re not looking for them to impersonate,” she explains. “We want their interpretation of the character. If they don’t know the series, oftentimes they have to go ask around a bit and talk to people in their lives.”
paras.zh: 但雅各布森表示，加入已建立的特许经营权并不总是立即得到肯定。 “肯定有一些人不太了解这个系列，所以我们需要对他们进行相关教育，并确保他们知道我们并不是在寻找他们来模仿，”她解释道。 “我们想要他们对这个角色的诠释。如果他们不知道这个系列，通常他们就必须四处打听，并与生活中的人交谈。”

paras.en: Culkin and Fanning, who play Caesar Flickerman and Effie Trinket, have been candid about finding their own interpretations while respecting the characters Stanley Tucci and Elizabeth Banks originated.
paras.zh: 扮演凯撒·弗利克曼和艾菲·特琳克的卡尔金和范宁坦率地寻找自己的诠释，同时尊重斯坦利·图齐和伊丽莎白·班克斯所创造的角色。

paras.en: “What we tell people who are new to it, and I really do believe this quite earnestly, is that it’s one of the very few franchises where, for each of the renowned actors we cast, it is actually all about performance. It’s never about prosthetics or visual effects,” Jacobson says. (Well, almost never: “Of course we use those things sparingly here and there. Those are not Glenn’s teeth,” she notes.)
paras.zh: “我们告诉刚接触这部电影的人，我确实非常认真地相信这一点，这是极少数的特许经营权之一，对于我们选拔的每一位知名演员来说，实际上一切都与表演有关。这与假肢或视觉效果无关，”雅各布森说。 （嗯，几乎从来没有：“当然，我们到处都很少使用这些东西。那些不是格伦的牙齿，”她指出。）

paras.en: The appeal, she says, is the creative freedom that comes with everything being “rooted in performance.” “You’re going to be collaborating closely with Francis and the department heads on the creation, building and design of your character, and it’s going to come down to meaty character work. You’re very rarely against a green screen. You’re almost always in a practical location with, hopefully, some other amazing actors in the scenes with you. I think these movies give each actor a real showcase of their talents, in a way that isn’t always true in a lot of other franchises.”
paras.zh: 她说，吸引力在于一切都“植根于表演”所带来的创作自由。 “你将与弗朗西斯和部门负责人密切合作，创作、构建和设计你的角色，这将归结为丰富的角色工作。你很少会面对绿幕。你几乎总是在一个实际的场景中，希望场景中还有其他一些出色的演员和你在一起。我认为这些电影让每个演员都真正展示了他们的才华，而这在许多其他系列中并不总是如此。”

paras.en: Jacobson recalls Sunrise on the Reaping being an “incredibly emotional” read. “I cried quite a few times, and then cried quite a lot at the end. I found it so fully moving and satisfying on so many levels.”
paras.zh: 雅各布森回忆说，《收割日出》是一本“令人难以置信的情感”读物。 “我哭了好几次，最后哭了很多次。我发现它在很多层面上都非常令人感动和满足。”

paras.en: But how do you adapt a book fans haven’t been able to read yet? The creative team relied on being fans themselves.
paras.zh: 但是，如何改编一本粉丝还无法阅读的书呢？创作团队依靠的是粉丝本身。

paras.en: “Nina and I consider ourselves fans, so there are a lot of things we fight to keep from the book, details we love ourselves,” Lawrence says. “And Suzanne is obviously going to fight for certain things: making sure her themes, ideas, the spirit of the characters and their emotional arcs are there. So there’s a good group of us there to protect what we think fans are going to love.”
paras.zh: “尼娜和我都认为自己是粉丝，所以我们努力从书中保留很多东西，包括我们自己喜欢的细节，”劳伦斯说。 “苏珊娜显然会为某些事情而奋斗：确保她的主题、想法、角色精神和情感弧线都在那里。所以我们有一群很好的人来保护我们认为粉丝会喜欢的东西。”

paras.en: “The funny thing is, it’s incredibly easy for me to know how fans will feel, because I’m the OG fan,” Jacobson says. “I’m as obsessed with the books as any diehard fan, and so is Francis.”
paras.zh: “有趣的是，我很容易知道粉丝的感受，因为我是 OG 粉丝，”雅各布森说。 “我和任何铁杆粉丝一样痴迷于这些书，弗朗西斯也是如此。”

paras.en: Still, some things had to go. “If I put everything that’s in the book into the movie, the movie would be six hours long. You can’t do that,” Ray says.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，有些事情还是必须放弃。 “如果我把书中的所有内容都放入电影中，电影就会有六个小时长。你不能这样做，”雷说。

paras.en: Sunrise doubles the number of tributes competing in the Games, and the team knew they couldn’t explore every one in depth. “Getting to know the tributes and understanding potential allies and enemies is one of the parts of these movies people really enjoy and are invested in. So figuring out how to balance the 48, and making sure we gave time and attention to the core characters whose stories are connected to Haymitch’s journey, was a definite challenge,” Jacobson says.
paras.zh: 《日出》使参加奥运会的贡品数量增加了一倍，团队知道他们无法深入探索每一个贡品。 “了解致敬内容并了解潜在的盟友和敌人是这些电影中人们真正喜欢和投入的部分之一。因此，弄清楚如何平衡这 48 个角色，并确保我们为那些故事与黑密斯的旅程相关的核心角色投入时间和注意力，是一个明确的挑战，”雅各布森说。

paras.en: The book is also told entirely from Haymitch’s point of view, which posed its own challenge. “What we found even in the original movies with Katniss was that if she wasn’t in a scene, the scene still needed to be about her in some way,” Jacobson says. “But when you’re only ever with that one person, there’s important context and opportunities you might miss. So figuring out where to break with his point of view, when to show something he can’t see or know, was a big decision in the adaptation process.”
paras.zh: 这本书也完全从黑密斯的角度讲述，这也提出了自己的挑战。 “我们发现，即使在凯特尼斯的原版电影中，即使她不在某个场景中，该场景仍然需要以某种方式讲述她，”雅各布森说。 “但是，当你只和那个人在一起时，你可能会错过重要的背景和机会。因此，弄清楚在哪里打破他的观点，何时展示他看不到或不知道的东西，是适应过程中的一个重大决定。”

paras.en: As for every other decision, the guiding principle was Collins.
paras.zh: 至于其他所有决定，指导原则都是柯林斯。

paras.en: “At the very beginning of the process, I asked Suzanne, ‘What is this book about for you?'” Ray recalls. “She talked about the philosophy of the book: the philosophy of propaganda and implicit submission, the philosophy of Thomas Hobbes, David Hume and John Locke. And I said, ‘Suzanne, what’s the book about for you emotionally?’ She said, ‘It’s about love and loss.’ I said, ‘Great, that’s what I’m writing.’ So anything that didn’t stick to that had to go.”
paras.zh: “在这个过程的一开始，我问苏珊，‘这本书对你来说是什么？’”雷回忆道。 “她谈到了这本书的哲学：宣传和含蓄服从的哲学，托马斯·霍布斯、大卫·休谟和约翰·洛克的哲学。我说，‘苏珊娜，这本书在情感上对你来说是什么？’她说，‘这是关于爱和失去的。’我说，‘太好了，这就是我正在写的。’所以任何不符合这一点的东西都必须去掉。”

paras.en: The Haymitch audiences meet in Sunrise is a far cry from the broken alcoholic of the original films. In Sunrise, audiences encounter a teen initially easygoing and unconcerned with politics. But his life transforms when he is forced into the 50th Hunger Games. Refusing to simply comply, he attempts to disrupt the Capitol’s system and oppose President Snow, altering both his own destiny and the world around him.
paras.zh: 观众在《日出》中遇到的黑密斯与原版电影中的酗酒者相去甚远。在《日出》中，观众遇到了一个最初很随和、不关心政治的青少年。但当他被迫参加第 50 届饥饿游戏时，他的生活发生了变化。他拒绝简单地服从，试图破坏国会大厦的制度并反对斯诺总统，从而改变自己的命运和周围的世界。

paras.en: Jacobson likens the young Haymitch to the “kind of guy who’s probably not very serious about school and is just waiting for the end of the day to run down to the beach with his surfboard and his girlfriend, hang out and catch some waves.” His attitude, as she sees it: “I can’t do anything about this broken world that I live in, but I’ve got a girl I love and a family I love, and that’s enough for me. Who am I? What difference would I make anyway?”
paras.zh: 雅各布森将年轻的黑密斯比作“那种可能对学校不太认真的人，只是等待一天结束时带着他的冲浪板和他的女朋友跑到海滩，闲逛并乘浪。”在她看来，他的态度是：“我对我生活的这个破碎的世界无能为力，但我有一个我爱的女孩和一个我爱的家庭，这对我来说就足够了。我是谁？我能带来什么改变呢？”

paras.en: Jacobson sees Haymitch’s arc as similar to Katniss’, with a priority on family that grows to include their community and district. “Your circle of concern grows in each movie, and there’s a cost to expanding that circle, a price to pay… But it’s the things he hears and brings with him from Lenore Dove. He says the Capitol has all the power and always will, and she says that doesn’t mean they always have, and it doesn’t mean they always will. It’s this notion that it’s not a foregone conclusion that oppressive power structures can’t be disrupted and ultimately destroyed.”
paras.zh: 雅各布森认为黑密斯的发展轨迹与凯特尼斯的相似，优先考虑的是家庭，逐渐扩大到包括他们的社区和地区。 “你的关注圈在每部电影中都会扩大，扩大这个圈子是有代价的，需要付出代价……但这是他从莱诺尔·多夫那里听到并带来的东西。他说国会大厦拥有所有权力并且永远都会，而她说这并不意味着他们永远拥有，也不意味着他们永远会拥有。这种观念认为，压迫性权力结构不能被瓦解并最终摧毁，这并不是一个已成定局的结论。”

paras.en: The Haymitch of the film faces a dilemma: “What am I willing to give up for the people I care about? And what am I willing to give up to right these really profound wrongs and try to end the Games?”
paras.zh: 影片中的黑密斯面临着一个困境：“为了我关心的人，我愿意放弃什么？为了纠正这些真正深刻的错误并试图结束奥运会，我愿意放弃什么？”

paras.en: “Seeing him get radicalized, and seeing him decide, even with all this loss, that the way to honor these people is to continue to fight: that was what was really important to me, and what I found really interesting and moving,” Lawrence says.
